video_title: Mark Walter Is DESPERATE - Could the Dodgers Be Next? - Mason & Ireland

quotes.speaker: John Ireland
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Walter's failed attempt to exit local TV deal
quotes.excerpt: Mark Walter apparently went to Charter Communications to see whether the company wanted to exit its local TV deal

text_blocks.speaker: John Ireland
text_blocks.text: According to John Orand of Puck, who is basically a media business insider, Mark Walter apparently went to Charter Communications to see whether the company wanted to exit its local TV deal for the Lakers and Dodgers several years early in exchange for a lump-sum payment, but those talks went nowhere.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris 'Sedano' Sedano
text_blocks.text: Mark Walter, hey Mark, you are talking to a media company. You are asking a media company for a lump-sum payment? Brother, you are out of your mind.

quotes.speaker: John Ireland
quotes.summary_phrase: Speculation on Mark Walter selling the Dodgers
quotes.excerpt: Mark Walter in all likelihood is going to have to get out of the Dodgers also.

text_blocks.speaker: John Ireland
text_blocks.text: If all of what you are reading is true, and by the way it is probably not, but some of it maybe is, Mark Walter in all likelihood is going to have to get out of the Dodgers also.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris 'Sedano' Sedano
text_blocks.text: I don't see a scenario where the assets that Mark Walter owns is probably not going to be under the control of Mark Walter for very soon, it seems like.

quotes.speaker: John Ireland
quotes.summary_phrase: Jeanie Buss's miscalculation regarding Mark Walter's finances
quotes.excerpt: Her biggest screw up in all of this was the assumption that Mark Walter has the money.

text_blocks.speaker: John Ireland
text_blocks.text: The story of the Buss family gets involved in all of this because obviously we all know the story by now that the five brothers and sisters they want to sell, they all say we are out. Jeanie says no, you don't have the power to do that. We are hanging on. Her biggest screw up in all of this was the assumption that Mark Walter has the money.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris 'Sedano' Sedano
text_blocks.text: They keep about 18 percent, which is roughly about 3 percent per bus family member.

quotes.speaker: John Ireland
quotes.excerpt: He has 1.1 billion coming due in about 6 weeks.

text_blocks.speaker: John Ireland
text_blocks.text: He has 1.1 billion coming due in about 6 weeks because his holding company tried to buy Clear Channel Outdoor. He also 6.5 billion to insurance regulators by December 31st. So in 90 days he owes 7.6 billion.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris 'Sedano' Sedano
text_blocks.text: So you see the thing is that when you are a billionaire, you think that you have the money.

quotes.speaker: John Ireland
quotes.summary_phrase: Misconceptions about billionaire team owners' liquidity
quotes.excerpt: There is this assumption from the regular guy, the little guy, that they have the money.

text_blocks.speaker: John Ireland
text_blocks.text: We look at these guys who buy teams and we all just think that they have the money. Like Bob Iger and Josh Kushner are going to buy the Lakers at a valuation of 12.5 billion dollars. There is this assumption from the regular guy, the little guy, that they have the money. It is not like that. Bob Iger doesn't have 12.5 billion dollars in his bank account to go write a check.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris 'Sedano' Sedano
text_blocks.text: Neither does Josh Kushner. You have to raise money, borrow money, bring in other partners.

quotes.speaker: John Ireland
quotes.summary_phrase: Dodgers' deferred money strategy and liquidity requirements
quotes.excerpt: For you to defer that money, you have to prove that you have it liquid.

text_blocks.speaker: John Ireland
text_blocks.text: We all know that the Dodgers have famously deferred money. It is my understanding that Major League Baseball says for you to defer that money, you have to prove that you have it liquid.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris 'Sedano' Sedano
text_blocks.text: Ohtani is the big fish here in regards to deferred money. But it is not just him, 50 million to Will Smith, 57 to Freddie Freeman, 65 to Blake Snell, 115 to Mookie Betts, Justin Turner is still owed 6 million next year, to Teoscar Hernandez 8.5 million, and Tommy Edman 25 million for a grand total of over 1 billion dollars.

quotes.speaker: John Ireland
quotes.summary_phrase: Major League Baseball's responsibility for deferred contracts
quotes.excerpt: Major League Baseball is to blame for allowing anybody, but in this particular case Mark Walter, to do these types of contracts.

text_blocks.speaker: John Ireland
text_blocks.text: Then if that is the case, then Major League Baseball is to blame for allowing anybody, but in this particular case Mark Walter, to do these types of contracts, which oh by the way is part of the reason they are going to go to a lockout.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris 'Sedano' Sedano
text_blocks.text: How can they go out and get a Teoscar Hernandez? How can they go spend 60 million dollars on Kyle Tucker? How is it that they are able to go get an Edwin Diaz?

quotes.speaker: John Ireland
quotes.summary_phrase: Incentives for players to accept deferred money
quotes.excerpt: It allows you to continue to live a lifestyle that you've been accustomed to.

text_blocks.speaker: John Ireland
text_blocks.text: Why do you suppose, forget Ohtani, why do you suppose a guy like Freddie Freeman, who is not somebody who makes a lot of money on endorsements, would defer 57 million dollars from 2028 to 2040? Why would somebody be inspired or incentivized to do that?

text_blocks.speaker: Chris 'Sedano' Sedano
text_blocks.text: No different than Bobby Bonilla, the famous one with the Mets. You have money coming in when you are no longer a player and it allows you to continue to live a lifestyle that you've been accustomed to.

quotes.speaker: John Ireland
quotes.summary_phrase: The critical nature of Mark Walter's financial situation
quotes.excerpt: The big story is what in the world is going on with Mark Walter.

text_blocks.speaker: John Ireland
text_blocks.text: I am beginning to think that Jeanie and her brothers aren't the big story. Bob Iger and Josh Kushner aren't the big story. The big story is what in the world is going on with Mark Walter.

text_blocks.speaker: Chris 'Sedano' Sedano
text_blocks.text: It seems like he needs liquidity fast.

quotes.speaker: John Ireland
quotes.summary_phrase: Bill Simmons' speculation on Mark Walter's legal jeopardy
quotes.excerpt: It started to seem like he might actually go to jail.

text_blocks.speaker: John Ireland
text_blocks.text: Here is Bill Simmons on his podcast talking about this. It started to seem like he might actually go to jail. He is already shed himself of the Lakers. He is selling his Chelsea stake reportedly right now, which was like 12.5 percent, and my guess is the Dodgers are going to be next. So what is this? Are we moving toward like a Bernie Madoff, Ivan Boesky type of situation?

text_blocks.speaker: Chris 'Sedano' Sedano
text_blocks.text: Will the words Mark Walter today plead guilty, will that sentence be said in the next two years?
